Class Fraction

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Number
be.imgn.gaia.core.math.Fraction
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<Fraction>
Direct Known Subclasses:
BigFraction, IntFraction, LongFraction
public abstract sealed class Fraction extends Number implements Comparable<Fraction> permits IntFraction, LongFraction, BigFraction
An exact fraction, always in lowest terms and with a positive denominator: an IntFraction, a LongFraction or a BigFraction, which differ by the size of their terms. 
Fraction chance = chances.of(7);                        // an IntFraction
chance.compareTo(BigFraction.of(1, 6)) == 0;            // true: fractions of any size compare by value
chance.toBigFraction().pow(3);                          // 1/216
chance.doubleValue();                                   // 0.16666666666666666

This class has what the three have in common whatever their size: comparing, converting, arithmetic, and the methods of Number.

An operation on two fractions returns a fraction of the larger of their two classes: an IntFraction and a LongFraction give a LongFraction. Each class also has the same operations on fractions of its own class, which return that class, so that the result of IntFraction.plus(IntFraction) is known to be an IntFraction. A result that doesn't fit in its class throws ArithmeticException: it isn't given a larger class.

Fractions of any classes compare by value, but only fractions of the same class are equal, as an Integer never equals a Long: compareTo may return zero for fractions that equals tells apart.

Since:
0.2.0
